documented_range.note: NO EVIDENCE ESTABLISHES THAT THIS PARTICULAR BUILDING EXISTED. It is the roof a reconstructed household requires - a sawpit and its shed on the river bank west of the built blocks: two men, a pit, a whip-saw and a stack of boards. NOT A MILL - no mill in the town is attested and none is claimed. The argument for the trade's presence in the town is in the household record and in the occupation census at data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json; the argument for THIS BUILDING is only that the household needs somewhere to be.

change_note: Raised by the inferred-household programme. A better-evidenced named building substitutes for this roof rather than standing beside it.

placement.position_note: INTERPRETIVE PLACEMENT, NOT A RECOVERED LOT. A sawpit and its shed on the river bank west of the built blocks: two men, a pit, a whip-saw and a stack of boards. NOT A MILL - no mill in the town is attested and none is claimed. The band follows ROADMAP K1's placement rule - businesses toward the river and the built streets, residences further out - using the same frontage bands the reconstruction recipes already work in, which come from the 80 ft platted street module in data/traces/street_control.json. The centre was tested against every structure footprint in the dataset, against the reserved slots of the two uninstantiated phase-2 recipes, against the platted street corridors of the K7 block grid so that no invented building stands in the roadway, and against the committed heightfield for coverage, dry ground and step tolerance; it is free ground and nothing more. The dataset's 20 m working georeference uncertainty applies on top of an already invented position.

residents.name: The Lynch household — a reconstructed sawyer (south division)
residents.why: inf_sawpit_shed is a structure record this parcel raises for the purpose, because no roof of the right family stood free in this district. The workplace is assigned from the reconstruction schedule's workshop and store families for this trade.
residents.basis: THIS BUILDING IS IN THE MODEL BECAUSE OF THIS HOUSEHOLD. Neither is documented: the household is inferred from the town's demonstrable needs and the roof was raised to house it. Its existence, position and size are all inventions, and the chips above say so.

persons.name: James Lynch
persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. THE NAME IS INVENTED TOO, and `name_basis` beside it says so and says which pool it came from: this record used to carry a bare designation instead, on the reasoning that a surname would make it look like the documented layer, but a town of designations does not read as a town and the grade, this note and name_basis all say plainly which layer this is. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). THE FIRST OF 2 SAWYER HOUSEHOLDS THIS LAYER RECONSTRUCTS. Asahel Pierce, building his smithy in October 1833, 'was obliged to haul his material from Plainfield, forty miles', because no suitable lumber could be had in Chicago (Andreas, scan p. 1161). Two years later the town is framing in sawn boards at a rate of hundreds of roofs a year. Some of that lumber came in by schooner and some was cut here; two sawyer households are inferred, the smallest number that answers the demand, and they work a sawpit on the river rather than a mill, because no mill in the town is attested.

residents.research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD - first of 2 sawyer households in this layer, in the south division. Asahel Pierce, building his smithy in October 1833, 'was obliged to haul his material from Plainfield, forty miles', because no suitable lumber could be had in Chicago (Andreas, scan p. 1161). Two years later the town is framing in sawn boards at a rate of hundreds of roofs a year. Some of that lumber came in by schooner and some was cut here; two sawyer households are inferred, the smallest number that answers the demand, and they work a sawpit on the river rather than a mill, because no mill in the town is attested. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.

what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED BUILDING, RAISED FOR A RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). A sawpit and its shed on the river bank west of the built blocks: two men, a pit, a whip-saw and a stack of boards. NOT A MILL - no mill in the town is attested and none is claimed. It is NOT one of the anonymous count-units of the 665-roof programme: those are placed by aggregate mix and carry no occupant, while this one exists because the occupation census says the town held a household of this trade and no anonymous roof of the right family stood free in this district. It consumes one slot of its district's programme target rather than adding to it - see the accounting block in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json.
